skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog:
- Improved process lock handling in session_check.sh to ensure better prevention of concurrent script execution.
- Updated logic for cleaning up expired lock files, increasing script reliability and avoiding deadlocks.
- Minor code cleanup for robustness.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior largely matches its stated purpose (scanning OpenClaw sessions and writing extracted items to Feishu), but there are several incoherences and secret-handling risks you should address before installing.

dimensions.detail: The scripts and SKILL.md consistently implement scanning OpenClaw session files and writing results to Feishu (L2/L3/L4). However the registry metadata at the top of the submission (Requirements: none / Required env vars: none / required binaries: none) does not match the included skill.json and SKILL.md, which declare required environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) and dependencies (openclaw, python3, bash). This metadata mismatch is an inconsistency that could lead to accidental misconfiguration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The scripts read local OpenClaw session files and call the local openclaw agent/CLI to perform AI extraction and to call Feishu tools—this is coherent with the stated purpose. However the script writes a prompt file (/tmp/ai_prompt_...) that contains session metadata and injected environment variable values (app tokens and doc IDs) and does not delete that prompt file after use, leaving secrets and possibly session contents in /tmp. The prompt also instructs the agent to call Feishu tools with the token embedded, which increases the risk of credentials appearing in logs or outputs. The scripts also log AI output and write background logs (/tmp/extract_*.log).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install/download is used; the skill is instruction + shell scripts that run locally. This is lower risk in terms of supply-chain downloads. The scripts do assume system tools (openclaw CLI, python3, bash, jq/inotify-tools mentioned in README) are present; those are reasonable for the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested environment variables are limited to Feishu credentials and IDs, which are appropriate for a skill that writes to Feishu. However: (1) the initial registry summary incorrectly stated there are no required env vars, inconsistent with the skill's own files; (2) the scripts embed tokens/IDs into the AI prompt file and pass them to the agent, which may expose secrets to agent logs or outputs and leaves the prompt file in /tmp; (3) notifications and file writes could leak conversation contents to Feishu—this is expected given the purpose but should be an explicit privacy decision for the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal agent invocation. The skill creates local files (markers in workspace/memory and temp files in /tmp) and uses a lock in /tmp; it does not request system-wide persistent privileges or modify other skills. Background invocation and cron-style scheduling are expected for this automation use case.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement what it claims (scanning OpenClaw session files and writing extracted items to Feishu), but take care before installing: 1) Do not use with sensitive or regulated conversations—the script will read all session files and push content to Feishu. 2) The skill requires Feishu credentials and IDs (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID); the registry summary mistakenly omitted these—ensure you supply only least-privilege tokens. 3) The extraction prompt (containing session info and the tokens) is written to /tmp and is not deleted — update the scripts to (a) use a secure mktemp with restrictive permissions, (b) delete the prompt file immediately after use, or preferably pass the prompt via a secure stdin pipe rather than writing tokens into a file or the prompt body. 4) Avoid embedding raw tokens in prompts; instead configure the openclaw Feishu tool/auth so the agent can use stored credentials without exposing them in prompts. 5) Review and secure logs (/tmp/extract_*.log and other logs) since they may contain session contents. 6) Verify openclaw agent/tool permissions: ensure the agent's Feishu actions are limited to the specific app/table/doc IDs you intend. If you cannot accept these risks or cannot modify the scripts, run the skill in an isolated environment or do not install it.
